title: Practice Any Hard Conversation Before It Matters
lesson: Skill acquisition needs rehearsal of the actual conversation, not only consuming information about it. The visual argument transfers boxing practice to an upcoming sales call.
opening: A presenter challenge rejects watching boxing videos and immediately entering the ring. Gym and ring images make the familiar skill gap concrete before it is applied to work.
story_arc: Boxing analogy → passive workplace training → knowledge/performance distinction → roleplay product → scheduled sales call → human/avatar rehearsal → claimed feedback and repeat attempt → broader uses → watch-versus-practise callback → comment CTA.
payoff: The comparison delivers a clear reason to rehearse and a recognisable practice interface. It does not demonstrate responsive pushback, personalised correction or measured improvement; the analytics insert is engagement data.
selection_reason: Shows a complete analogy-to-scenario structure, repeated presenter returns, paired human/interface splits, one precise calendar spotlight, an accumulating scope graphic and a closing visual callback. It also shows where plausible imagery fails to prove the exact words.
review_limits: Complete chronological 2 fps contextual sheets were visually inspected, with narrow calendar and presenter strips sampled every sixth decoded source frame and a full-resolution analytics frame. The strip manifests record source frame indices and PTS from the native scan. No audio audition in this expansion; spoken ideas are paraphrases from timed caption sidecars checked against visible context. Boundaries are approximate editorial partitions, generally within 0.5-second contextual spacing; exact-index strips refine only inspected intervals. Exact easing and word lock are not claimed. The automatic transcript extends past the 43.933333-second visual rendition, so coverage ends at the observed media duration. These are source observations and planning guidance, not a rendered replica or qualified template.
